# Feature: Explicit managed update

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-046
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_puppeteer_browser_management.md`

`yantra browser update` is the **only** place in Yantra that ever asks whether a newer Chrome exists. Nothing else — not startup, not `run`/`resume`/`ask`/`research`/`do`, not the recorder, not `init`, `doctor`, `browser list`, `browser use`, or `browser check`, not the scheduler, the daemon, or a nested workflow — resolves Chrome for Testing metadata, ever. There is no schedule, no reminder, no background probe, and no stored "last checked" timestamp.

The command has exactly two modes:

- **`yantra browser update --dry-run`** — availability only. Resolve current Stable, compare it with the locally recorded managed build, print the answer, change nothing. It takes no lease, needs no consent, cannot download, and is not blocked by a running managed browser.
- **`yantra browser update [--yes]`** — consented replacement. It requires an existing managed installation, refuses while a managed browser is running, asks before replacing on a TTY, then acquires the **exact build the user consented to** and publishes it atomically as the single managed installation. The build it replaces becomes an orphan and is collected.

Three plan corrections shape this feature and must not be re-derived:

- **The availability mode is spelled `--dry-run`, never `--check`** (§5). `yantra config data-dir --dry-run` already owns that spelling for "report what this command would do without doing it", and `browser check` already means a local compatibility probe with no network — the opposite of an availability query. One word meaning two opposite things inside one noun namespace is exactly the failure memory's flag-vocabulary rule exists to prevent.
- **There is no transaction phase machine and no crash-recovery routine** (§7.5). Publication is one atomic pointer write; any `installation-*` child the pointer does not name is an orphan. A killed update leaves an orphan, the next explicit `install`/`update` collects it, and the user never sees a "your last update did not finish" state — there is nothing they could do about it and nothing unsafe about it.
- **A build newer than Puppeteer's tested pairing is the normal case** (§7.3, §10). Every managed build this command installs will normally sit outside the `152.0.7977.75` pairing, so `capability-checked` is reported as ordinary provenance and never as a warning.

The closing constraint, stated once: **this feature builds no second acquisition path.** FEAT-044 already owns the helper process, preflight, candidate naming, verification, atomic publication, and orphan collection. FEAT-046 adds Stable resolution, the comparison, busy refusal, and the command surface — and calls FEAT-044's transaction for everything else.

Generating this specification runs no browsers, no downloads, no tests, and changes no source.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

`.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist, and plan §4 forbids creating one for browser downloads: no relational schema, no migration, no version history, no registry. This section defines only what FEAT-046 adds on top of FEAT-043's contracts (`ManagedReadyRecord`, `ManagedReadySnapshot`, `ManagedStateReader`, `ManagedCoordinator`, `ManagedMutationLease`, `CompatibilityResult`, `DriverCompatibilityDescriptor`) and FEAT-044's install types (`DownloadConsentRecord`, `ManagedInstallPhase`, `ManagedInstallProgress`, `ManagedInstallFailureCode`, `ManagedInstallPolicy`, `OrphanCollectionReport`, `ManagedSelectionNotice`, `HelperRequest`).

### Entities & Attributes

**Stable resolution** — one metadata answer, never cached to disk. There is deliberately no `lastCheckedAt` field and no availability cache file: a stored timestamp is the seed of a background-check feature, and plan §5 forbids reminders, schedules, and background checking outright.

```ts
interface StableBuild {
  readonly buildId: string; // e.g. '153.0.8010.36'
  readonly platform: ManagedReadyRecord['platform'];
  readonly resolvedAt: string; // ISO; in-memory provenance for this invocation only
  readonly artifactAvailable: boolean; // canDownload() for this exact build and platform
}

type StableResolution =
  | { readonly status: 'resolved'; readonly build: StableBuild }
  | { readonly status: 'unavailable'; readonly error: ManagedUpdateError };

interface StableResolutionService {
  /** Metadata only. Never downloads, never writes, never takes a lease. */
  resolveStable(options?: {
    readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
    readonly deadlineMs?: number; // defaults to ManagedInstallPolicy.metadataMs
  }): Promise<StableResolution>;
}
```

**Update comparison** — a closed union over "what is installed" versus "what is available". `installed-newer` exists because plan §7.5 forbids a silent downgrade; it is a report, not a failure.

```ts
type UpdateComparison =
  | {
      readonly state: 'no-installation';
      readonly available: StableBuild;
      readonly installCommand: 'yantra browser install';
    }
  | {
      readonly state: 'up-to-date';
      readonly installed: ManagedReadyRecord;
      readonly available: StableBuild;
    }
  | {
      readonly state: 'update-available';
      readonly installed: ManagedReadyRecord;
      readonly available: StableBuild;
    }
  | {
      readonly state: 'installed-newer';
      readonly installed: ManagedReadyRecord;
      readonly available: StableBuild;
    };
```

Ordering uses `getVersionComparator(Browser.CHROME)` from the pinned `@puppeteer/browsers`, which is a public export — do **not** hand-roll a dotted-version compare beside it. Memory: a validation or ordering grammar duplicated across layers is silent divergence, not redundancy.

**Availability report** — what `--dry-run` renders. It reads a local snapshot plus one metadata call and owns nothing.

```ts
interface ManagedUpdateAvailability {
  readonly comparison: UpdateComparison;
  readonly managedRoot: string;
  readonly driver: { readonly version: string; readonly testedBuild: string };
  readonly concurrentOperation: boolean; // a live mutation lease exists — reported, never acted on
  readonly activeManagedRun: boolean; // reported so the user knows a replacement would refuse
  readonly nextCommand: string | null; // 'yantra browser update' / 'yantra browser install' / null
}
```

**Update request and outcome** — the mutation mode. `consent` is FEAT-044's record type, extended rather than duplicated (see Indexes & Constraints).

```ts
interface ManagedUpdateRequest {
  readonly consent: DownloadConsentRecord; // names the exact target build in `replaces`/`targetBuildId`
  readonly target: StableBuild; // resolved once, before consent; never re-resolved after
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
  readonly onProgress?: (event: ManagedInstallProgress) => void;
  readonly deadlineMs?: number;
}

type ManagedUpdateOutcome =
  | {
      readonly status: 'replaced';
      readonly previousBuildId: string;
      readonly record: ManagedReadyRecord;
      readonly executablePath: string;
      readonly compatibility: CompatibilityResult;
      readonly orphans: OrphanCollectionReport;
      readonly selection: ManagedSelectionNotice;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'up-to-date';
      readonly record: ManagedReadyRecord;
      readonly available: StableBuild;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'installed-newer';
      readonly record: ManagedReadyRecord;
      readonly available: StableBuild;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'cancelled';
      readonly at: ManagedInstallPhase;
      readonly retainedOrphan: string | null;
      readonly record: ManagedReadyRecord;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'failed';
      readonly error: ManagedUpdateError;
      readonly record: ManagedReadySnapshot;
    }; // proves the prior installation survived

interface ManagedUpdateService {
  /** Metadata + local comparison only. No lease, no mutation, no download. */
  checkAvailability(): Promise<ManagedUpdateAvailability>;
  /** Consented replacement. Refuses when no managed installation exists or a managed run is live. */
  update(request: ManagedUpdateRequest): Promise<ManagedUpdateOutcome>;
}
```

**Failure taxonomy** — FEAT-044's `ManagedInstallFailureCode` is reused verbatim and extended with exactly two update-only codes. There is **one** managed-acquisition failure taxonomy, not two.

```ts
type ManagedUpdateFailureCode =
  | ManagedInstallFailureCode // unsupported-platform, metadata-unavailable, proxy-failure,
  // network-failure, extraction-failure, timed-out,
  // verification-failure, compatibility-failure, … (FEAT-044 §2)
  | 'no-managed-installation' // update requires one; directs to `yantra browser install`
  | 'managed-run-active'; // a managed browser is running; stop it and retry

interface ManagedUpdateError {
  readonly code: ManagedUpdateFailureCode;
  readonly phase: ManagedInstallPhase | 'comparing';
  readonly remediation: string; // one supported repair, rendered verbatim
  readonly detail: string; // sanitized; never raw helper stderr or an archive command line
  readonly proxyHost?: string; // credentials stripped
  readonly retainedOrphan: string | null;
  readonly activeRunPids?: readonly number[]; // present for 'managed-run-active'
}
```

**Helper protocol extension** — `--dry-run` and pre-consent resolution must reach the Chrome for Testing metadata host **through the configured proxy**, and plan §6 establishes that `@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.2` bypasses `HTTPS_PROXY` in-process because it imports `proxy-agent` optionally and does not declare it. The routing fix is `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` on the owned helper, so metadata resolution runs in that same helper rather than in the CLI process — setting a process-wide proxy flag on the whole CLI is not an option.

```ts
// Extends FEAT-044's HelperRequest. protocolVersion goes 1 -> 2.
type HelperMode = 'install' | 'resolve';

interface HelperRequest {
  readonly protocolVersion: 2;
  readonly mode: HelperMode; // 'resolve' resolves Stable and exits; it never downloads
  readonly operationId: string;
  readonly browser: 'chrome';
  readonly platform: ManagedReadyRecord['platform'];
  readonly cacheDir: string | null; // null and rejected-if-present in 'resolve' mode
  readonly buildId: string | null; // required in 'install' mode for an update; null resolves Stable
  readonly progressIntervalMs: number;
}

// HelperMessage gains one variant; the rest are FEAT-044's.
type HelperResolveMessage = {
  readonly kind: 'availability';
  readonly buildId: string;
  readonly artifactAvailable: boolean;
};
```

Bumping `protocolVersion` rather than making `mode` optional is deliberate: the parent and the helper always ship from the same `dist/`, a version mismatch already means `helper-unavailable`, and memory permits clean internal breaks in this pre-release repository. An optional field would let a stale helper silently perform an install when a resolve was requested.

### Relationships

- One managed root holds at most one **ready record**, 0..1 **live mutation lease**, and 0..N orphans. A successful update creates exactly one new `installation-<opaque-id>` child, atomically repoints the pointer at it, and turns the previous child into an orphan. No promotion, no rename, no common-ancestor deletion, and no second selectable build at any instant.
- One update operation resolves Stable **exactly once**, before consent, and installs precisely that `buildId`. Consent and acquisition therefore name the same build even if upstream publishes a new Stable mid-operation.
- One update operation spawns 0..1 **resolve** helper and 0..1 **install** helper; the install helper's 0..2 descendants are FEAT-044's enumerated set (an extraction tool, plus `setup.exe` on Windows).
- `--dry-run` holds **no** lease and **no** reservation, so a live mutation or a running managed browser is reported as local state and never blocks it.
- One update touches **zero** external installations and **zero** config keys. The configured selection is read for the selection notice and never written.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Consent is one type, extended, not duplicated.** FEAT-044's `DownloadConsentRecord` gains `targetBuildId: string` and `replaces: string | null`, and its `ConsentSource` union gains `'cli-update-prompt'`. A separate update-consent type would be a second grammar for the same decision.
- **Availability is never persisted.** No file, no cache entry, no config key, no timestamp records that a check happened or what it found. A test asserts that a `--dry-run` run leaves the data and cache roots byte-identical.
- **No downgrade, ever.** `installed-newer` reports both identities and leaves the installation intact; it is exit 0 in both modes and is never rendered as a failure or a prompt.
- **Metadata failure never disables a working browser.** An unresolvable Stable is an _update_ error only. The recorded ready pointer, the compatibility evidence cache, and every launch path are untouched, and a subsequent offline launch of the installed managed browser must still succeed.
- **Busy is checked twice.** `hasActiveUse()` is consulted before any metadata call in mutation mode, and the exclusive lease is claimed and re-verified immediately before the replacement phase, so a browser started during the download cannot race the publish. Both refusals are `managed-run-active`.
- **`--dry-run` and `--yes` are conflicting modes** (plan §5), rejected as a validation error rather than tolerated: an acceptance flag on a command that cannot act is a dead control, and memory forbids dead controls.
- **`browser update` registers no browser-selection options.** `--browser` and `--browser-path` are rejected as unknown: this command always operates on the managed installation and can honor neither.
- **Deletion stays FEAT-044's.** Orphan collection is called, never reimplemented: exact recorded relative path under canonical containment with symlinks and junctions resolved, never the managed root, its parent, the coordination directory, the pointer's own child, or a common ancestor.

### TASK-005: Refuse replacement while a managed browser is running

- [ ] **Implementation**: In `managed-update.ts`, consult `ManagedCoordinator.hasActiveUse()` **before** any metadata call in mutation mode and return a typed `managed-run-active` error carrying the owning PIDs and stop-and-retry guidance — detecting after a 200 MB download is a wasted download. Claim the exclusive mutation lease and **re-verify** absence of active use immediately before the replacement phase, closing the race where a browser starts during the transfer; a lease held by another operation surfaces as `operation-in-progress`. Never terminate a running managed browser and never wait indefinitely for one to exit. Uncertain owner liveness fails conservatively: refuse rather than authorize a deletion. External launches are unaffected throughout, and a new managed launch during a live mutation refuses with `operation-in-progress` through FEAT-043's existing contract — this task adds no second lock and no second liveness rule.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: With real bounded processes rather than mocked async functions — an update attempted while a managed run holds a reservation is refused before any metadata call, naming the PIDs; a managed run started _after_ the busy check but before the replacement phase is caught by the re-verification and the update aborts leaving the previous pointer intact and one collectable orphan; two simultaneous updates leave one pointer, one child, and one caller refused with `operation-in-progress`; a managed launch during a live update mutation refuses while an external launch in the same window succeeds; a reservation whose owner died is not treated as live and does not deadlock the update; a reservation whose liveness is uncertain refuses conservatively; no running browser is ever terminated by an update (assert the child process is still alive after the refusal); a killed update owner leaves an orphan that the next explicit `install` or `update` collects.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for why an update refuses while a browser is running and what the user does about it.
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/browser/managed-update-concurrency.spec.ts`. Every liveness assertion observes an actual process, per plan §9 rule 3.
- **Depends on**: TASK-004.

- [ ] **Implementation**: Complete the `update` subcommand's mutation branch. Order of operations: precondition check (`no-managed-installation` → exit 3 naming `yantra browser install`), busy check (`managed-run-active` → exit 3 with the PIDs and stop-and-retry guidance), resolve Stable once, compare. `up-to-date` and `installed-newer` print the verdict and exit 0 with no prompt and no download. Map outcomes to the existing exit-code map: success and both no-op verdicts 0, missing acceptance 1, declined or cancelled 4 through the user-handoff convention, every environment and contention failure 3 with its own remediation. ### TASK-007: Preserve prior readiness through every failure and interruption

- [ ] **Implementation**: Close the failure semantics across `managed-update.ts` and the command. Any failure or cancellation before publication leaves the ready pointer untouched, the previous installation selectable and launchable, and the candidate as an orphan; the `failed` and `cancelled` outcomes carry the surviving `ManagedReadySnapshot` so the caller can state that plainly. There is **no** recovery routine, no phase machine, no resume, and no user-visible "your last update did not finish" state — a killed operation simply leaves an orphan that the next explicit `install`/`update` collects (plan §7.5). Cancellation reuses FEAT-044's bounded cancellation, including the non-interruptible Windows `setup.exe` window: report cancelling rather than cancelled while it blocks, honor the cancel the instant it returns, and release coordination and delete nothing until verified descendant exit. A `metadata-unavailable`, `proxy-failure`, or `network-failure` is an update failure only and must leave the installed browser fully usable offline. Emit structured Pino events for the availability check, the comparison verdict, consent source and target build, each phase transition, busy refusal, cancellation, orphan collection result, and failure class — never launch arguments, raw helper stderr, archive command lines, environment, credentials, or task payloads.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: A failure injected at each phase — preflight, metadata, download, extraction, finalize, verification, probe, publication — leaves the previous pointer intact, the previous executable still resolvable and launchable, and exactly one collectable orphan; the next explicit `install` or `update` collects that orphan and reports the bytes reclaimed; cancellation during download and during extraction leaves no live helper and no live descendant, asserted by the descendant's own exit; cancellation arriving during the blocking finalize phase is reported as in-flight while it blocks, honored immediately after, and never reported complete during the block; a killed update owner produces no user-visible recovery concept anywhere in the CLI, `doctor`, or the JSON envelopes (assert no output string suggests resuming or repairing); after a metadata failure the installed managed browser launches offline; log events carry the declared fields and none of the forbidden ones; a failed update never reports success while an orphan exists, and orphans are never selectable because selection reads the pointer.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for what happens when an update fails or is interrupted — the previous browser keeps working and space is reclaimed on the next explicit command.
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/browser/managed-update.spec.ts tests/browser/managed-update-concurrency.spec.ts`. Each case asserts the previous installation is still launchable, not merely that a pointer file exists.
- **Depends on**: TASK-005, TASK-006.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No credential, keychain entry, or provider session is involved, and no model is invoked. Proxy credentials are read from the environment, never stored, and stripped from every message, log, and envelope.
- **Consent**: Replacing a browser is a user decision, never an engine inference. The update service accepts only a `DownloadConsentRecord` whose `targetBuildId` matches the resolved target, constructible only by `--yes` or a terminal prompt; its absence means no download. Consent authorizes one operation against one named build and is never persisted or reused. `--dry-run` needs no consent because it changes nothing, and it rejects `--yes` rather than exposing an acceptance flag with no effect.
- **Error handling**: Missing acceptance is validation (exit 1), as are `--dry-run --yes` and unsupported flags. Declined consent and cancellation are user-handoff outcomes (exit 4) that change no installation and no selection. No managed installation, an active managed run, contention, unsupported hosts, missing prerequisites, disk, permission, proxy, network, metadata, extraction, verification, and compatibility failures are environment failures (exit 3), each naming what was observed and one supported repair. Two failure codes must never render identical user text, and no message may imply that a version mismatch alone caused a failure. `up-to-date` and `installed-newer` are successes, not failures.
- **Logging**: Structured Pino events for the availability check and its verdict, resolved and installed build identities, consent source and target build, phase transitions, busy refusal with owner identity, cancellation, orphan-collection result with bytes reclaimed, and failure class. Never log launch arguments, raw helper stderr, archive command lines, the environment, credentials, or task payloads. A `capability-checked` pairing is a structured event and command output, never a per-invocation warning — an always-on warning is a warning nobody reads, and after this command it will be the normal state.
- **Security and ownership**: Only validated, canonically contained Yantra-owned paths are written or deleted; external installations and user-owned binaries are never modified or removed, and a symlink or junction escape cannot widen a deletion. `installDeps` stays pinned `false`, `expectedHash` stays unset by the recorded §6 decision, `baseUrl` is never passed and ambient download-override variables are stripped, TLS verification stays on, no shell interpolation or privilege escalation occurs, and Yantra's own helper and termination processes are hidden on Windows. Browser selection is untouched: this command writes no config key. No model-visible update capability is added — the agent cannot request, trigger, or observe an update.
- **Offline and update policy**: This feature owns the only update-metadata call in the product. It has no schedule, no reminder, no background path, and no persisted availability state — deliberately not even a "last checked" timestamp, because that is the seed of the background-check feature plan §5 forbids. Every other surface stays offline, and an installed managed browser remains fully usable with no network at all.
- **Testing**: Vitest AAA behavior tests, `@no-llm` tagging, boundary mocks only at external boundaries, and real bounded processes wherever the claim is about processes. Assert observable outcomes — files on disk, the process that exited, the proxy that received the request — never call shapes. Targeted runs are `cd packages/<pkg> && npx vitest run <path>`; `e2e` reads core from built `dist/`, so build before trusting it; a real-browser test that passes alone may need its own timeout allowance under full-suite contention.
